question.worked_solution:
Interpreting the fractions as division, we get

$$
(15\,÷\,4)\times (16\,÷\,3).
$$

 

Since our expression contains multiplication and division only, we can create an equivalent expression by swapping the $÷\,4$ and $÷\,3$:

 

$$
(15\,÷\,3)\times (16\,÷\,4)
$$

 

Interpreting the divisions as fractions, we get

$$
\frac{15}{3}\times \frac{16}{4}.
$$

Carrying out the divisions, we arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}{{\frac{15}{3}}_{⏟}}_{5}\times {{\frac{16}{4}}_{⏟}}_{4}=5\times 4=20.\end{aligned}
$$
